newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says it increasing internal security.
newsitem.headline: Israel says it increasing internal security.

text.p: Israel said on Saturday it was further increasing security in its towns and cities and along lines bordering the West Bank and Gaza Strip after Wednesday's twin suicide bombing in Jerusalem.

Police spokesman Linda Menuhin said the decision to step up security, already boosted following the fatal bombings, had been taken by Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani and Israeli police chief Assaf Hefetz.
The Islamic militant bombers killed 13 other people when they blew themselves up in Jerusalem's main Jewish market on Wednesday in the worst attack in Israel for more than a year.
"After consultation, Mr Kahalani and the police commissioner decided to reinforce police forces in crowded areas all over the country," Menuhin said.

More checkpoints would be set up and activities by Israeli civil guards boosted "in order to foster security". Kahalani and Hefetz had also urged Israelis to be more alert to potential threats, Menuhin said.

It was not immediately clear whether the step was taken in response to a demand for the release of all Palestinian prisoners by Sunday night made in a leaflet that claimed the attack on Wednesday. The leaflet was issued in the name of the militant Hamas movement but Israeli officials say they are not certain it is authentic.
